I am an undergraduate researcher at Jeonbuk National University, majoring in
Statistics with a minor in Mathematics, and applying to PhD programs in
Statistics and Biostatistics.

Most of my work so far has been on health data, but what pulls me into a problem
is usually the statistical question rather than the subject area — whether a
method still holds once its assumptions are loosened, and whether a result
survives being moved somewhere new. That has taken me into weather time series
and network models as readily as into hospital records.

## Education

**B.S. in Statistics**, minor in Mathematics — Jeonbuk National University (JBNU) \
March 2021 – February 2027 (expected)

**Visiting Student** — University of Nevada, Las Vegas \
UNLV summer research program (EIP) · Four weeks, June – July 2025 \
Credit-bearing program in machine learning and data science, combining coursework
with a team research project.

## Research experience

**Cross-country transfer learning for ICU admission prediction** — ongoing \
Transfer of a TabPFN-based clinical prediction model across countries, with target
adaptation and a label-noise analysis.

**Deep neural networks for mortality prediction from EHR** — UNLV, 2025 \
Compared interpolation schemes and network architectures on irregularly sampled
vital-sign sequences from a Brazilian cancer center.

**Neural Granger causality for solar radiation data** — JBNU, 2025 \
Applied component-wise MLP and LSTM models to a year of hourly meteorological
observations, benchmarked against a linear VAR.

**Digital cognitive training for dementia: a meta-analysis** — 2025 \
PROSPERO-registered systematic review and meta-analysis of eleven randomized
controlled trials.

Full descriptions are on the [Research](research.qmd) page.
